newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. execs see economy doing well - NYT poll.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. execs see economy doing well - NYT poll.

text.p: Nearly nine out of 10 senior executives at U.S. companies think the country's economy is doing well, up from nearly half who said the same thing four years ago, according to the results of an opinion poll published Friday.
The New York Times, which commissioned the poll with CBS News, said 80 percent of them described the economy as "fairly good" and 11 percent as "fairly bad".
It said 48 percent of those surveyed did not see the economy going into a recession until after 1998, while another 27 percent expected it to happen during that year.
It said 26 percent of the 442 executives interviewed by telephone said the federal deficit was the most important economic problem facing the country, while another 9.0 percent said taxes were.
The newspaper said 49 percent said they planned to increase their work force in 1998, while the other 45 percent would keep it steady.
It said 63 percent would increase capacity at their companies and 34 percent would hold it at the current level.
The newspaper said half of the executives intended to make major investments in new technology next year and 26 percent planned to make no "major" investments.
It said 50 percent of those polled projected profits holding steady and 34 percent saw them rising.
The newspaper said polling firm Survey Sampling Inc conducted the survey between September 25 and October 11.
It did not give a margin of error.
